Actor.description: `[[actors]]` — one named worker in the project.

name.description:
Unique actor name; the value an `assignee:` field (or a
`[tasks.assignee] allowed` entry) references.

roles.description: Roles the actor holds, each naming a declared `[[roles]]` entry.

oneOf.description: A person.
A language model.

comments.description:
Whether the scaffold carries explanatory `#` comments — the header block
and the per-slot annotations (kind, required/optional, choices, default).
`true` (default) keeps them; `false` strips every comment, leaving a bare
mapping of slot names to values.

editor.description:
Editor command override. Falls back to `$VISUAL`, then `$EDITOR`, then a
built-in default. May carry arguments (split on whitespace).

header.description:
Scaffold header override. Absent uses the built-in instructions; an empty
(or all-blank) string disables the header; any other text replaces it,
comment-prefixed so it stays valid YAML. Ignored when `comments = false`.

Anchor.description: One labeled point in an anchor classification.

color.description: Optional color: a named ANSI color or `#RRGGBB`.

value.description: The point on the scale this label names.

AssigneeConfig.description: `[tasks.assignee]` — who may be named, and whether one must be.

allowed.description: Allowed assignees (the project's actors). Empty = accept any value.

example.description:
The assignee `mt check` files a spliced slot with. A required assignee
with no `example` leaves that slot unfillable.

required.description: Whether an assignee must be set.

values-when.description:
A filter naming the tasks held to `allowed`; every other task keeps
whatever it carries. Absent holds every task.

Band.description: One contiguous labeled range in a band classification.

color.description: Optional color: a named ANSI color or `#RRGGBB`.

max.description: Upper bound (inclusive for int and the last real band; else exclusive).

Category.description: One category: the expression that selects it, its score and its display.

color.description: Optional color: a named ANSI color or `#RRGGBB`.

label.description: Display label; falls back to empty when absent.

score.description: Score of a task in this category, used for bands and sorting.

when.description:
Boolean expression over the inputs. A task falls in this category
when it is true.

CheckSpec.description:
`check = { typst, function, field }` — a `[[tasks.rules]]` entry that calls
a Typst function instead of evaluating an `assert` expression.

field.description:
Field whose value the function receives (`none` when the task omits
it). Absent means the function receives the whole task, in the shape
`mt eval --json` prints.

function.description: Name of the function `typst` exports that this rule calls.

typst.description:
Path to the Typst module exporting `function`, relative to the project
root (the directory holding `.mindtape/`).

Checker.description:
One `[[tasks.waits]]` entry: a named command that answers whether a task
still waits.

name.description: The name a `waits-on` entry writes before its colon.

run.description:
The command line, with `{id}` standing for the entry's id. It runs
through `sh -c`, or `cmd /C` on Windows, from the project root. Exit 0
means the wait is over, 1 means it goes on, anything else is unknown.

oneOf.description: Each folder name as an independent flat tag (`backend`, `auth`).

Cumulative path prefixes joined by the separator (`backend`,
`backend:auth`).

when.description:
Condition under which this column renders. It takes the `[[ls.rules]]`
condition grammar (`tty()`, `format()`, `env()`, `on_branch()`,
`now()`, `weekday()`, `true`, `false`) plus four listing predicates:
`nonempty()`, `contested()`, `named()` and `blocked()`. Absent means
the column never renders.

CommentsConfig.description: `[tasks.comments]` — review-comment policy over a task's whole source file.

allow-pattern.description:
Regex permitting a deliberate comment form — matched against the
comment's stripped, trimmed inner text — even under `warn`/`forbid`.

policy.description: Whether a comment is unconstrained, reported, or fails `mt check`.

CommentsPolicy.description: How `mt check` treats a comment found in a task's source.

oneOf.description: Comments are unconstrained. The default.
A comment is reported but `mt check` still succeeds.
A comment is reported and fails `mt check`.

CommitRuleSpec.description: `[[commits.rules]]` — one assertion a checked commit must satisfy.

assert.description: Commit expression that must hold for every commit the rule applies to.

message.description:
What a breach tells the author, in place of the default advice naming
the `assert` expression.

name.description:
The name a report shows for the rule (`commits.rules.<name>`). The same
name overrides or `disable`s the rule across packs. Optional: an
unnamed rule reports by its position (`commits.rules[0]`).

scope.description: What the rule is evaluated over. Default `commit`.

severity.description: Whether a breach fails the check or only reports. Default `warn`.

when.description:
Commit expression gating which commits the rule applies to. Absent
means every commit.

CommitScope.description: What a commit rule is evaluated over.

oneOf.description: Once per commit, over its `subject`, `refs`, `files`, `trailers` and `tasks_only`.

Once per task the commit changes or names, over the commit's fields
plus `named` and the task as of `head(...)`, `staged(...)` and
`worktree(...)`.

Once per task any commit of a range names, over the task as the
range's newest commit holds it, in the filter language of
`[[tasks.rules]]`. Only `mt check --commits` runs it; a task the tip
lacks is skipped.

CommitsConfig.description:
`[commits]` — how commits name the tasks they work on, and the rules a
commit is checked against.

rules.description: `[[commits.rules]]` — assertions every checked commit must satisfy.

trailer.description:
The trailer key whose values name tasks by stem (`Refs: <stem>`).
Matched case-insensitively. A value that is a path, or names no task,
is always refused.

ContentAssert.description: The assertion made over a matched section's content: the string `"non-empty"`, or a one-key table `{ min-words = N }`, `{ max-words = N }`, `{ must-match = "regex" }`, `{ must-not-match = "regex" }`, or `{ density = { pattern = "regex", max = N, per = "section" } }`.

min-words.description: The section must contain at least this many words.

max-words.description: The section must contain at most this many words.

must-match.description: Rust regex the section's source text must match.

must-not-match.description: Rust regex the section's source text must not match.

rules.description: Ordered list of section-content gating rules.

ContentRuleConfig.description:
One entry in `[[tasks.body.content.rules]]`.

`path` selects sections by heading path, the same way a header rule does.
`assert` is checked against each matched section's content. Like a header
rule, it takes an optional `when` filter and `message` override.

assert.description: The assertion made over each matched section's content.

message.description: Override for the default violation message.

name.description:
The name a report shows for the rule (`body.content.rules.<name>`).
Optional: an unnamed rule reports by its position instead
(`body.content.rules[0]`). Two rules in this array sharing a name is a
config error naming both.

path.description: Path through the heading tree selecting the sections to assert over.

when.description: Optional filter expression gating this rule to matching tasks only.

DedupMode.description: `mt add`'s collision policy when the destination stem already exists: `fail` bails before writing, `skip` exits 0 without writing and reports the existing path, `add-suffix` mints `-2`, `-3`, … until a free stem turns up. `mt add --dedup` overrides this for one run; see `[tasks.naming] dedup` for the unset default.

DensitySpec.description:
`{ density = { pattern, max, per } }` — fails when one unit of the section
carries more than `max` matches of `pattern`.

max.description: The most matches of `pattern` a single unit may carry.

pattern.description: Rust regex counted within each unit.

per.description:
Unit to count matches in: `section` (the default), `paragraph` or
`sentence`.

DensityUnit.description: Unit a `density` assert counts matches in: `section` (the default), `paragraph` or `sentence`.

breadcrumb-root.description:
Whether breadcrumb tags start with the root name (`mt`, `mt:backend`,
…).

collect.description:
Collectors to run. Both may run at once; their tags are merged
without duplicates.

enabled.description: Default derivation switch for roots that set no `derive-tags` of their own.

slugify.description: Normalize folder names to tag form.

anyOf.description: Enable or disable for every file under the root.
Enable only for files matching this glob.
Enable only for files matching any of these globs.

DeriveTags.description:
Per-root tag derivation: a bool, a file glob, or a list of globs. `true` or
`false` turns derivation on or off for every file under the root. A glob
turns it on only for files whose path, relative to the root, matches.

DictCase.description: How a compiled dictionary compares a lookup against its entries.

oneOf.description:
ASCII-case-insensitive: a capitalised title word matches a lowercase
entry. The default.
Byte equality.

DictSpec.description: `[dicts.<name>]` — one named string set, as declared in config.

case.description:
How a lookup compares against the entries: `fold` (the default) is
ASCII-case-insensitive, `exact` is byte equality.

include.description:
Other dictionaries — project or built-in — whose entries are unioned in.
The entries arrive raw; this dict's own `case` decides how they compare.

path.description:
A file of entries, one per line, relative to the project root. Blank
lines and lines whose first non-blank character is `#` are skipped, and
each entry is trimmed. May leave the root (`../shared/verbs.txt`), the
same rule `[[typst.local-packages]] path` follows.

EstimateConfig.description: `[tasks.estimate]` — the legal estimate units and whether one is required.

example.description:
The estimate `mt check` files a spliced slot with, as `unit = quantity`
pairs. A required estimate with no `example` leaves that slot
unfillable.

required.description: Whether an estimate must be set.

units.description: Allowed unit names. Empty = any unit.

FallbackSeverity.description:
`[templates] fallback-severity` — how a breach of the built-in template
reports.

oneOf.description: Print the breach; `mt check` still succeeds. The default.
Print the breach and fail `mt check`.

FieldConfig.description:
`[tasks.fields.<name>]` — allowed values, default and requirement for
`kind` or one `x-<ns>` extension field.

default.description:
Value `mt add` fills in when the field is required and neither the
template nor the caller sets it. `mt check` never applies it.

example.description:
The value `mt check` files a spliced slot for this field with: a string,
or a list of strings for a `multiple` field. A required field with no
`example` and no `default` leaves that slot unfillable, so
`mt check` names this table.

multiple.description:
Whether an `x-<ns>` field holds a list of strings rather than one
string. `mt check` refuses a string in such a field, and a list in a
field with `values` that does not declare it. `mt add` offers the field
as a multi-choice slot.

required.description: Whether the field must be set.

values.description:
Allowed values. Empty accepts any value, and a non-empty list takes a
string, or a list of distinct strings for an `x-<ns>` field. An entry `@<dict>` stands for every entry of
`[dicts.<dict>]`, so the list may mix literal values and dictionaries.

values-when.description:
A filter naming the tasks held to `values`; every other task keeps
whatever it carries. Absent holds every task.

anyOf.description: The example of a single-valued field.

FieldExample.description:
A `[tasks.fields.<name>] example`: one string, or a list for a `multiple`
field.

FlipAction.description:
One action of an `[[on.flip]]` entry. Set exactly one of `show`, `list`
and `run`, or set `gate = true` with no `run`.

gate.description:
Whether a non-zero exit from `run` refuses the flip. With no `run`, the
gate refuses every flip the entry's `when` matches. Applies to a `run`
action or a gate with no `run`.

list.description: `{ list = "filter or @view" }` — print the matching tasks.

message.description:
Explanation printed when `run` exits non-zero, or when a gate with no
`run` refuses the flip.

run.description:
`{ run = "command" }` — run a command through the platform shell
(`sh -c`, or `cmd /C` on Windows). A gating action may omit it; then
the gate refuses the flip whenever the entry's `when` matches.

FlipHook.description: One `[[on.flip]]` entry: which transitions it fires on, and what it does.

actions.description: Actions to run, in declaration order.

when.description:
Filter over the task being flipped, plus `into("status")` for the status
being stamped. Empty fires on every flip.

FormatConfig.description: `[format]` — how `mt` canonicalizes task source before writing it.

enabled.description:
Whether `mt` runs typstyle over the Typst source it writes (`add`,
`flip`, `review`, `recur`, `import`), so every write leaves the file in
one formatted shape. `true` by default. With `false`, `mt` changes only
the bytes it edits: diffs stay smaller, and stray body indentation can
build up.

Framework.description:
One scoring framework: typed inputs, plus either a `score` formula or a
list of categories.

category.description:
Categories to classify a task into. For any input values, exactly one
category's `when` must be true. Cannot be combined with `score`.

inputs.description:
Inputs by name. `score` and each category's `when` refer to them by
these names.

score.description:
Arithmetic expression over the inputs that computes the score, such as
`impact * confidence * ease`. Cannot be combined with `category`.

editor.description:
Editor command. `mt go` replaces a `{task}` token with the task's file
path, or appends the path when there is no token. Falls back to
`$VISUAL`, then `$EDITOR`; `mt go` fails when none is set. May carry
arguments, split on whitespace.

HeaderAction.description: What a heading rule checks: `require`, `forbid` or `unique` over `path`, `order` of `before` and `after`, or an `allowlist` of headings.

HeaderPathSegment.description: One step in a heading path: an exact string (direct-child match) or `{ match = "regex", recursive = bool }`.

match.description: Rust regex matched against heading text.

recursive.description: Match any descendant (true) or only direct children (false).

HeaderRuleConfig.description:
One entry in `[[tasks.body.headers.rules]]`.

`action` selects what the rule checks and which fields apply.
- `require` / `forbid` / `unique` — how many headings `path` matches.
- `order` — `before` headings must precede `after` headings.
- `allowlist` — under `scope` (the top level when omitted), only `allowed`
  headings may appear.

action.description:
Whether the target headings must exist, must not, or must be unique, or
whether this is an `order`/`allowlist` rule.

after.description: Path whose headings must come after (`order`).

before.description: Path whose headings must come first (`order`).

message.description: Override for the default violation message.

name.description:
The name a report shows for the rule (`body.headers.rules.<name>`).
Optional: an unnamed rule reports by its position instead
(`body.headers.rules[0]`). Two rules in this array sharing a name is a
config error naming both.

scope.description:
Path selecting scopes whose children are constrained (`allowlist`);
omit to constrain top-level headings.

when.description: Optional filter expression gating this rule to matching tasks only.

rules.description: Ordered list of heading gating rules.

HyperlinkChoice.description:
`[ls] hyperlinks` — whether the `#` and `file` cells carry OSC 8
hyperlinks to the row's `hyperlink-target`. The `--hyperlinks` flag takes
the same values.

A terminal without OSC 8 support can print the escape sequence as visible
text, and no terminal reports whether it supports OSC 8. That is why the
default is `never`.

oneOf.description: Enable hyperlinks only when stdout is a TTY and `TERM` is not `dumb`.
Always emit OSC 8 hyperlink sequences.
Never emit hyperlink sequences.

format.description:
Format an explicit `id:` must have. The default, `string`, accepts any
non-empty string.

IdFormat.description: Format requirement for an explicit task `id:` field.

Input.description: One declared input: its type and bounds (numbers) or allowed values (enums).

InputKind.description: The type of a framework input.

oneOf.description: A bounded number.
A boolean.
A string from a fixed set of values.

InteractiveMode.description: When `mt add` opens the interactive editor.

oneOf.description: Open in a terminal when a required slot is still unfilled (default).
Always open in a terminal; error when stdin/stdout is not a TTY.
Never open; behave as the non-interactive pipeline.

Legend.description:
The status legend: the legal status values, in lifecycle order.

Each entry gives a value its glyph, color, label and `terminal` flag. An
empty legend (`status = []`) accepts any status. Omitting
`[[tasks.status]]` takes the shipped six-status legend.

LegendEntry.description: One `[[tasks.status]]` entry: a value plus its display attributes.

color.description: Optional color: a named ANSI color or `#RRGGBB`.

label.description: Optional display label; falls back to `value`.

note.description:
Whether a move into this status needs a note: `required` or
`optional` (the default). With `required`, `mt flip` refuses the move
without `-m`, and `mt check` flags a task here with no note.
`forbidden` is accepted but not enforced for a status.

terminal.description:
Whether this status ends a task. The `terminal` filter matches tasks in
it, and `mt` does not check their tags or estimate units.

to.description:
Statuses a task may move to from this one. While no entry sets `to`,
any move is allowed. Once any entry sets it, `mt flip` refuses a move
the legend does not list, and an entry with no `to` allows only a
same-status re-stamp. A terminal status reopens by listing the status
to reopen into.

unblocked.description:
Whether a task must be unblocked to enter this status. `mt flip`
refuses the move while a direct blocking target is unfinished, and
`--force` overrides. On a terminal status, every child must be
finished too. `mt check` warns about a blocked task already here. Off
by default. Set it where work starts or finishes, and leave it off
statuses that blocked work must still reach, such as `cancelled`.

value.description: The status name, as written in a task's `status:` field.

acyclic.description:
Whether edges of this kind must not form a cycle. Applies only when
`validate` is `local-task-path`, because only edges between tasks can
form one.

blocking.description:
Whether an unfinished target keeps the task from being ready. Applies
only when `validate` is `local-task-path`, because only a task can be
unfinished.

max.description: Most edges of this kind one task may carry. Absent means no limit.

name.description: Kind name, matched against an edge's `kind`.

note.description: Note requirement for edges of this kind.

regex.description:
Regex a target must match when `validate = "regex"`. That validator
requires it, and every other validator rejects it. A missing or invalid
pattern is a config error.

validate.description:
What this kind's targets are. The default, `local-task-path`, is a
path from the linking task's file to another task's file. Any other value makes the targets something outside the
backlog, such as a commit, a pull request or a build.

LinksConfig.description: `[tasks.links]` — the link kinds a task's `links:` edges may use.

kinds.description:
Custom link kinds, added to the built-in ones. A built-in kind cannot
be redefined.

LocalPackage.description: `[[typst.local-packages]]` — one `@local/<name>` package loaded from a project directory.

path.description: Directory holding the package's `typst.toml`, relative to the project root.

columns.description:
Per-column display settings, keyed by column name. The shipped
defaults set `when` on every column; a column with no `when` never
renders.

columns-order.description:
Explicit column order and selection: when set, only the listed
columns render, in that order. Empty (the default) keeps the built-in
column set and order.

contains-fields.description:
Fields that `contains()` searches when a call names none, in order.
Takes any filter field name, plus `body`, `note` and `tags`. Empty (the
default) searches `title`, `id` and `body`. A call that names its
field, such as `contains("x", note)`, ignores this key. An unknown name
is a config error.

date-format.description:
Date format for every date column. Tokens, longest match first: `YYYY`
4-digit year, `YY` 2-digit year, `MMMM` full month name, `MMM`
abbreviated month, `MM` zero-padded month, `M` bare month, `DD`
zero-padded day, `D` bare day. Other characters print as written.
Absent prints ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`.

default-sort.description:
Default sort chain for `mt ls` when the caller passes no `--sort`.
Same spec grammar as `--sort`: `"field"` or `"field:asc"` / `"field:desc"`.
Validated at config load. When absent the shipped built-in chain applies.

default-view.description:
Name of the view that drives the default `mt ls` listing when the
caller passes no filter: falls back to the `[views.default]` view when
this is unset, or matches every task when neither is declared.
Validated at config load.

hyperlink-target.description:
URI that a row's `#` and `file` cells link to. `mt` replaces `{abs}`
with the task's absolute path and `{rel}` with the path the `file`
column shows. Defaults to `file://{abs}`. Point it at another scheme,
such as an editor's URI handler, to open the task there.

hyperlinks.description:
Whether the `#` and `file` cells carry terminal hyperlinks: `auto`,
`always`, or `never` (the default). `--hyperlinks` overrides it for one
run.

overdue-color.description: Color for the overdue due-date accent. Defaults to `"red"`.

ready.description:
Glyph, color and label for the ready and blocked states in the `READY`
column. An unset key takes the shipped default.

rules.description:
Ordered auto-activation rules applied to a bare `mt ls` (no CLI
filter, no `@view`): the first rule whose condition holds (or that
has none) wins and supplies its filter, sort, and columns.

LsRule.description:
One `[[ls.rules]]` entry.

The first rule (top to bottom) whose `condition` holds — or that omits
`condition` entirely — drives the default `mt ls` listing. Its effective
facets are `import-views` composed left-to-right (per-facet last-wins),
then any manual `filter` / `sort` / `columns` override (highest
precedence). All fields are optional; a rule with none of them still
matches (by an absent `condition`) but contributes no facets.

columns.description:
Manual column list — highest precedence for the columns facet. An
entry may reference a view's columns with `@view`.

condition.description:
Condition expression over environment predicates such as
`on_branch`, `env`, `weekday`, and `now`. Absent means the rule always
matches.

filter.description:
Manual filter override — highest precedence for the filter facet.
Same grammar as `[views]`; may use `@view` / `in_view`.

import-views.description:
Ordered list of views to import facets from, composed left-to-right
(later entries win on conflict). Each entry is a view name (`"view"`,
importing its filter, sort, and columns) or a scoped form
(`"view(filter, sort)"`) naming just the facets to import.

name.description:
Shown in the trailer and the JSON envelope's `applied.rule`; falls
back to the condition text when unset.

sort.description:
Manual sort override — highest precedence for the sort facet. Same
spec grammar as `--sort`; an entry may splice `@view`.

NamingConfig.description:
`[tasks.naming]` — how `mt add` and `mt recur` name a new task's file, and
what `mt add` does when that name is taken (`dedup`).

dedup.description:
What `mt add` does when the stem is taken; `--dedup` overrides it for
one run. Unset means `add-suffix` when `stem` is set, else `fail`.

stem.description:
Filename stem template. Macros: `{slug}`, `{date}`, `{date:FMT}`,
`{yy}`, `{mm}`, `{dd}`, `{n}` and `{n:0N}`. Unset means `{slug}`.

NoteRule.description: Note requirement for an edge kind.

oneOf.description: A non-empty note is required, as on the built-in `related` kind.
A note is allowed but not required (the default).
A note is rejected.

NumericField.description:
A numeric scalar field: a `[min, max]` scale plus, optionally, one
classification style — contiguous bands or labeled anchor points.
Defaults to an integer `0..9` scale with no classification.

example.description:
The value `mt check` files a spliced slot with. A required field with
no `example` leaves that slot unfillable.

kind.description: Whether the scale is integer or real.

required.description: Whether the field must be set.

OnConfig.description: `[on]` — hooks keyed by the event that fires them.

PriorityConfig.description:
`[tasks.priority]` — the priority scale and its scoring frameworks.

It takes the same scale, bands and anchors as `[tasks.difficulty]`. When
`framework` names a framework, `mt` computes a task's priority from that
framework's inputs. `allow-manual` decides whether a raw integer is still
accepted. `frameworks` holds the built-in frameworks merged with any the
project declares.

allow-manual.description: Whether a raw integer is accepted while a framework is active.

example.description:
The value `mt check` files a spliced slot with. A required field with
no `example` leaves that slot unfillable.

framework.description:
Name of the framework that computes priority, a key of `frameworks`.
Absent means priority is a raw number.

frameworks.description:
Scoring frameworks by name: the built-in ones merged with any declared
here.

kind.description: Whether the scale is integer or real.

required.description: Whether the field must be set.

code.description: Short project qualifier. Falls back to the root directory name when absent.

ReadyConfig.description:
`[ls.ready]` — glyph, color and label for the ready and blocked states in
the `READY` column. An omitted key takes the shipped default.

blocked-color.description: Color for the blocked state: a named ANSI color or `#RRGGBB`.

blocked-glyph.description: Glyph shown for a blocked task.

blocked-label.description: Display label for the blocked state.

ready-color.description: Color for the ready state: a named ANSI color or `#RRGGBB`.

ready-glyph.description: Glyph shown for a ready (unblocked, non-terminal) task.

ready-label.description: Display label for the ready state.

RecurConfig.description:
`[tasks.recur]` — whether recurring tasks are enabled, and the values a
`recur` field may take.

default-anchor.description: Anchor used when a task's `recur` omits one.

enabled.description:
Whether the recurrence feature is enabled. `false` rejects any
authored `recur` field outright, at both `mt check` and `mt recur`.

materialize.description: Materialize model used when a task's `recur` omits one.

rrule.description:
Whether a `recur` field may use `rrule(...)`. Off by default. Without
it, `mt` rejects an `rrule(...)` with an error.

Requirement.description: Whether a field is required: `false` (never), `true` (always), or a filter expression matching exactly the tasks that must carry it (e.g. `"!terminal"` — required until the task reaches a terminal status).

RetireConfig.description: `[retire]` — the gitless `rm` tombstone: keep the file, flip the status terminal.

rename.description:
Move the retired task file into a sibling folder of this name, such as
`.archive`. Omitted keeps the file where it is.

status.description: The terminal status the retired task flips to; defaults to the legend's first terminal status (an error if the legend declares none).

default-filter.description:
Filter selecting which tasks a bare `mt rm` (no target given) retires.
Defaults to `"terminal"`, sweeping every task in a terminal status.
An explicit ref or filter argument on the command line overrides it.

strategy.description: How inbound references to a removed task are handled; defaults to `"git-tombstone"` in a git repository, `"reject"` without one.

RmStrategy.description: How `mt rm` handles links from other tasks to a removed task.

oneOf.description: Mint a git-pinned SWHID tombstone and rewrite inbound edges onto it (the default in a git repo).
Keep the task file, flip it to a terminal status — a tombstone without git.
Strip each inbound edge from the surviving tasks, then delete.
Refuse, listing every surviving task that references a removed task.

Role.description:
`[[roles]]` — one role name an actor can hold. A role carries no settings;
a harness keys its own config by role name.

RootConfig.description: The table form of a task root.

derive-tags.description: Tag derivation for this root. Absent takes `[tasks.derive-tags] enabled`.

name.description: Tag emitted for the root itself. Defaults to the path's last segment.

path.description: Directory (relative to the project root) holding one task per file.

RootSpec.description:
One `[[tasks.roots]]` entry: a bare path string, or a table with a root
tag name and a per-root tag derivation rule. A list may mix both forms.

RuleSpec.description:
`[[tasks.rules]]` — one assertion or check every selected task must
satisfy. Set exactly one of `assert` and `check`.

assert.description:
Filter expression that must evaluate true for every task the rule
applies to. Exactly one of this and `check` is set.

check.description:
A Typst function to call instead of an `assert` expression. Exactly
one of this and `assert` is set.

message.description:
What an `assert` breach tells the author to do, in place of the
default advice naming the `assert` expression. A `check` rule ignores
it and prints each string its function returns.

name.description:
The name a report shows for the rule (`rules.<name>`). Optional: an
unnamed rule reports by its position instead (`rules[0]`).

severity.description: Whether a breach fails the command or only reports. Default `warn`.

when.description:
Filter expression gating which tasks the rule applies to. Absent means
every task.

ScaleKind.description: Whether the scale carries integers or reals.

oneOf.description: Whole numbers; bands are inclusive and contiguous.
Real numbers; bands are half-open, the last one closed.

Severity.description: How a breached config-declared constraint reports.

oneOf.description: Print the breach; the command still succeeds. The default.
Print the breach and fail the command.

allowed.description:
Allowed tag names. Empty accepts any tag. The loader derives folder tags
again on every load, so a moved file gets its new folder's tags. An entry
`@<dict>` stands for every entry of `[dicts.<dict>]`.

values-when.description:
A filter naming the tasks held to `allowed`. Absent means `!terminal`,
so a closed task keeps a tag dropped from the list.

TargetValidator.description:
What shape a link kind's targets take — the `validate` key of
`[[tasks.links.kinds]]`.

oneOf.description:
A path from the linking task's file to another task's file (the
default, and the only validator whose edges join the task graph).
An RFC 3986 URI: a scheme, then only URI-legal characters.

A hexadecimal git object name, 7 to 64 characters — abbreviated SHA-1
through full SHA-256.

A UUID, hyphenated, as 32 bare hex digits, in braces, or with a
`urn:uuid:` prefix.
A project-supplied pattern, taken from the kind's sibling `regex` key.
Any non-empty text, with no shape check.

TasksConfig.description: `[tasks]` — where tasks live and how they are constrained.

assignee.description: Which actors `assignee:` may name, and whether it is required.

body.description: Rules over a task body's headings and section content.

comments.description: Review-comment policy over a task's whole source file (`mt check`).

difficulty.description: The difficulty scale and its labeled anchors or bands.

estimate.description: Allowed estimate units, and whether an estimate is required.

fields.description:
Allowed values, default and requirement for `kind` and for each
`x-<ns>` extension field, keyed by field name. Any other key fails
config load.

links.description: Custom link kinds that `links:` edges may use, beside the built-in ones.

naming.description:
The filename stem template `mt add` and `mt recur` use, and what
`mt add` does when the stem is taken (`dedup`).

priority.description:
The priority scale, its bands, and an optional scoring framework that
computes priority from inputs.

recur.description:
Whether recurring tasks are enabled, and the units, anchors and limits
`mt recur` accepts.

roots.description: Directories (relative to the project root) holding one task per file.

rules.description:
Assertions every selected task must satisfy. `mt check` enforces them,
and so does every write command before it writes.

status.description:
Status legend: legal values in lifecycle order, plus per-value display
(glyph, color, label) and the `terminal` flag.

tags.description: Tag allow-list, checked on open tasks only.

waits.description:
Commands a `waits-on` entry names: each answers by exit code whether a
task still waits on something outside the repo.

default.description: Template stem `mt add` uses when none is named.

dirs.description: Directories, relative to the project root, holding `*.typ` task templates.

fallback-severity.description:
How `mt check` reports a breach of the built-in template, which `mt add`
falls back to when no template dir holds `task.typ`. A project's own
templates always report errors.

local-packages.description:
`@local/<name>` packages to load from a directory in the project, so a
task can import a package that is not installed globally. `mt`
registers `@local/mindtape` itself when `<root>/lib` holds the
`mindtape` package; list any other package here.

columns.description:
Column set applied when this view drives columns (bundle mode or
`--columns @name`). Empty means the default column set.

filter.description:
Filter expression (the filter facet). May reference other views via
`in_view("other")` or the `@other` sugar. Empty means match-all.

sort.description:
Sort chain applied when this view drives sort (bundle mode or
`--sort @name`). Same spec grammar as `--sort`; empty means the default
order.

description: Schema for `.mindtape/config.toml`, the per-project Mindtape configuration. Every section is optional; an omitted section takes the shipped defaults.

actors.description:
The project's actor registry (`[[actors]]`): named workers (people and
language models) that `assignee:` values may reference.

commits.description:
`[commits]` — the task trailer and `[[commits.rules]]`, checked by
`mt check --commit-msg`.

dicts.description:
Named string sets (`[dicts.<name>]`), so a vocabulary two rules share is
one list rather than two that drift. Each unions `values`, `path` and
`include` into one set, compiled and checked once at config load. The
`mindtape-` prefix is reserved for the built-in dictionaries.

disable.description:
Rule names to drop once every pack and layer has added its rules. A
name that matches no rule is a config error.

extends.description:
Rule packs this config builds on, in any config layer. A name with the
reserved `mindtape-` prefix and no path separator is a pack built into
`mt`. Anything with a path separator is a TOML pack file, relative to
the file that declares it. A pack adds entries to `[[tasks.rules]]`,
`[[tasks.body.headers.rules]]`, `[[tasks.body.content.rules]]`,
`[[commits.rules]]` and `[dicts]`, ahead of this layer's own. A rule in
this layer replaces a pack rule with the same name.

format.description: Whether `mt` reformats the Typst source it writes (`[format]`).

on.description: Status-transition hooks (`[[on.flip]]`), run only by `mt flip`.

roles.description:
Role names (`[[roles]]`) that actors may hold. A role carries no
settings; a harness keys its own config by role name.

tasks.description: Task discovery, status lifecycle, and field constraints.

title: Mindtape project configuration
